content:
## Approach

The claims must stay byte-identical, so the new region has to enter through **defaulted XRD fields** plus a **second `ProviderConfig`**. Crossplane's default-injection happens at the API server (structural schema defaults), so every existing `XNetworkedApp` claim silently gets `region: us-east-1` and resolves to the same `providerConfigRef` it uses today — no diff, no re-reconcile churn.

---

## 1. Second ProviderConfig

`providers/providerconfig-us-west-2.yaml`

```yaml
apiVersion: aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-us-west-2
spec:
  credentials:
    source: IRSA          # same IRSA role as us-east-1; region is a resource-level field
---
apiVersion: aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
kind: ProviderConfig
metadata:
  name: aws-us-east-1
spec:
  credentials:
    source: IRSA
```

> Note: on `provider-aws` (upbound family) region is **not** part of `ProviderConfig` — it is `spec.forProvider.region` on each MR. The `ProviderConfig` split is still worth keeping because it gives per-region credential/role separation and a stable patch target if you later move to distinct IRSA roles per region.

---

## 2. XRD: additive, defaulted fields

`xrds/xnetworkedapp.yaml` (diff only)

```yaml
spec:
  versions:
    - name: v1alpha1
      served: true
      referenceable: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                environment:
                  type: string
                  enum: [dev, prod]
                # --- new, both defaulted ---
                region:
                  type: string
                  enum: [us-east-1, us-west-2]
                  default: us-east-1
                replicaRegion:
                  type: string
                  enum: [us-west-2]
                  default: us-west-2
              required:
                - environment      # region intentionally NOT required
```

`region` is absent from every existing claim → API server injects `us-east-1` → the rendered composed resources are unchanged. `required` is untouched, so no existing claim becomes invalid.

---

## 3. Composition: region-aware patches

`compositions/networkedapp-aws.yaml` (relevant entries)

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.crossplane.io/v1
kind: Composition
metadata:
  name: xnetworkedapp.aws
spec:
  compositeTypeRef:
    apiVersion: platform.example.io/v1alpha1
    kind: XNetworkedApp
  mode: Pipeline
  pipeline:
    - step: patch-and-transform
      functionRef:
        name: function-patch-and-transform
      input:
        apiVersion: pt.fn.crossplane.io/v1beta1
        kind: Resources
        resources:

          # ---------- primary bucket ----------
          - name: assets-bucket
            base:
              apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
              kind: Bucket
              spec:
                forProvider:
                  region: us-east-1
            patches:
              - type: FromCompositeFieldPath
                fromFieldPath: spec.region
                toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.region
              - type: FromCompositeFieldPath
                fromFieldPath: spec.region
                toFieldPath: spec.providerConfigRef.name
                transforms:
                  - type: string
                    string:
                      type: Format
                      fmt: "aws-%s"

          - name: assets-bucket-versioning
            base:
              apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
              kind: BucketVersioning
              spec:
                forProvider:
                  versioningConfiguration:
                    - status: Enabled
            patches: *regionPatches        # same two patches, anchored

          - name: assets-bucket-sse
            base:
              apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
              kind: BucketServerSideEncryptionConfiguration
              spec:
                forProvider:
                  rule:
                    - applyServerSideEncryptionByDefault:
                        - sseAlgorithm: AES256
            patches: *regionPatches

          - name: assets-bucket-pab
            base:
              apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
              kind: BucketPublicAccessBlock
              spec:
                forProvider:
                  blockPublicAcls: true
                  blockPublicPolicy: true
                  ignorePublicAcls: true
                  restrictPublicBuckets: true
            patches: *regionPatches

          # ---------- replica bucket (prod only) ----------
          - name: assets-bucket-replica
            base:
              apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
              kind: Bucket
              metadata:
                annotations:
                  crossplane.io/external-name: ""   # patched below
              spec:
                providerConfigRef:
                  name: aws-us-west-2
                forProvider:
                  region: us-west-2
            patches:
              - type: FromCompositeFieldPath
                fromFieldPath: spec.replicaRegion
                toFieldPath: spec.forProvider.region
              - type: FromCompositeFieldPath
                fromFieldPath: spec.replicaRegion
                toFieldPath: spec.providerConfigRef.name
                transforms:
                  - type: string
                    string: { type: Format, fmt: "aws-%s" }
              # dev renders nothing: environment != prod -> skipped by condition step
```

### Gating the replica on `prod`

`patch-and-transform` has no per-resource conditional, so the replica set is gated in the pipeline:

```yaml
    - step: prod-only-replication
      functionRef:
        name: function-cel-filter
      input:
        apiVersion: cel.fn.crossplane.io/v1beta1
        kind: Filter
        filters:
          - name: assets-bucket-replica
            expression: observed.composite.resource.spec.environment == "prod"
          - name: assets-bucket-replica-versioning
            expression: observed.composite.resource.spec.environment == "prod"
          - name: assets-bucket-replication
            expression: observed.composite.resource.spec.environment == "prod"
          - name: replication-role
            expression: observed.composite.resource.spec.environment == "prod"
```

Dev composites evaluate `false` → those resources are dropped from the desired state → **no dev state is touched**.

### Replication wiring

```yaml
          - name: replication-role
            base:
              apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
              kind: Role
              spec:
                forProvider:
                  assumeRolePolicy: |
                    {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[{"Effect":"Allow",
                     "Principal":{"Service":"s3.amazonaws.com"},"Action":"sts:AssumeRole"}]}

          - name: replication-policy
            base:
              apiVersion: iam.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
              kind: RolePolicy
              spec:
                forProvider:
                  policy: |
                    {"Version":"2012-10-17","Statement":[
                      {"Effect":"Allow",
                       "Action":["s3:GetReplicationConfiguration","s3:ListBucket"],
                       "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::SRC"},
                      {"Effect":"Allow",
                       "Action":["s3:GetObjectVersionForReplication",
                                 "s3:GetObjectVersionAcl",
                                 "s3:GetObjectVersionTagging"],
                       "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::SRC/*"},
                      {"Effect":"Allow",
                       "Action":["s3:ReplicateObject","s3:ReplicateDelete","s3:ReplicateTags"],
                       "Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::DST/*"}]}
            # SRC/DST substituted via CombineFromComposite patches on bucket names

          - name: assets-bucket-replication
            base:
              apiVersion: s3.aws.upbound.io/v1beta1
              kind: BucketReplicationConfiguration
              spec:
                providerConfigRef:
                  name: aws-us-east-1
                forProvider:
                  rule:
                    - id: assets-to-usw2
                      status: Enabled
                      priority: 1
                      deleteMarkerReplication:
                        - status: Enabled
                      destination:
                        - storageClass: STANDARD_IA
```

No wildcard actions, resource-scoped ARNs — satisfies the prod IAM criterion.

---

## 4. Claims: unchanged

`claims/dev.yaml` — **untouched**

```yaml
apiVersion: platform.example.io/v1alpha1
kind: NetworkedApp
metadata:
  name: web-dev
  namespace: dev
spec:
  environment: dev
  compositionRef:
    name: xnetworkedapp.aws
```

`claims/prod.yaml` — **untouched**

```yaml
apiVersion: platform.example.io/v1alpha1
kind: NetworkedApp
metadata:
  name: web-prod
  namespace: prod
spec:
  environment: prod
  compositionRef:
    name: xnetworkedapp.aws
```

Both acquire `region: us-east-1` and `replicaRegion: us-west-2` from schema defaults.

---

## 5. Verification before rollout

```bash
# 1. Render dev — must be byte-identical to the pre-change render
crossplane render claims/dev.yaml compositions/networkedapp-aws.yaml functions.yaml \
  > /tmp/dev-after.yaml
diff /tmp/dev-before.yaml /tmp/dev-after.yaml    # expect empty

# 2. Render prod — expect exactly the new us-west-2 resources added
crossplane render claims/prod.yaml compositions/networkedapp-aws.yaml functions.yaml \
  | yq '.spec.forProvider.region' | sort -u
# us-east-1
# us-west-2

# 3. Confirm no drift on live dev composites
kubectl get xnetworkedapp -l crossplane.io/claim-namespace=dev \
  -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.region}'   # us-east-1
```

---

## Why not the alternatives

| Option | Rejected because |
|---|---|
| New `Composition` for us-west-2 + `compositionRef` per claim | Requires editing every claim — violates the constraint |
| `compositionSelector` on labels | Still a claim edit (labels live on the claim) |
| Environment-specific `EnvironmentConfig` | Good for values, but region selection here needs to be per-composite and defaulted; an `EnvironmentConfig` lookup keyed on `spec.environment` would also work, and is the better move if you later need >2 regions |
| Hardcode `us-west-2` in the replica base with no XRD field | Works today, but makes the DR region invisible in the API and unpatchable per-claim later |

## Residual risks

- **`crossplane.io/external-name` collisions**: the replica bucket must get a distinct name. Bucket names are globally unique, so patch it as `<composite>-assets-replica`, not the same external-name as the primary.
- **Provider pod IRSA scope**: if the IRSA role's trust/permission boundary is region-scoped, `aws-us-west-2` will fail auth even though the `ProviderConfig` exists. Verify `s3:*Replication*` and `s3:PutObject` on the us-west-2 ARNs are in the role before applying.
- **Replication requires versioning on *both* buckets**, and it must be `Enabled` before `BucketReplicationConfiguration` reconciles. Add `crossplane.io/composition-resource-dependency` ordering or accept one reconcile loop of `ReconcileError`.
